title: When Done Well Why Schools Dont Improve
author: Carolyn Carousel
summary: Educational improvement initiatives often fail despite good intentions because schools lack the coherent implementation infrastructure to sustain change. When reforms are well-designed but poorly implemented, they create the illusion of action without actual progress. The critical factor determining school improvement is not whether initiatives are theoretically sound, but whether schools have the capacity to execute them consistently across classrooms. This analysis distinguishes between having good ideas and having the organizational systems necessary to turn those ideas into sustained teaching practice.
points: School improvement requires coherent implementation systems, not just well-designed initiatives
Good ideas without implementation infrastructure produce activity without progress
Most school reform failures stem from execution gaps, not design flaws
Sustained improvement depends on organizational capacity to maintain consistency across all classrooms
The design of change initiatives matters far less than the systems built to sustain them
